chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: 'If zakat is permissible for a man in the month of Ramadan, and he delays it until Muharram,' he said, 'There is no harm.' I said: 'And if it is only permissible in Muharram, and he hastens it in the month of Ramadan,' he said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.اَلْمُحَرَّمُ: Muharram (the first month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: Can I pay Zakat early or late in Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of zakat timing by confirming that neither hastening payment in Ramadan nor delaying it to Muharram is problematic, provided the obligation is fulfilled. This ruling underscores the principle of *ease* (taysir) in Shia jurisprudence, allowing believers to align financial worship with personal convenience or seasonal liquidity without incurring sin. The permissibility of both early and late payment highlights that the strict temporal boundaries are guidelines for obligation rather than rigid constraints on the act of purification itself.
